subject: PolarisAI onboarding: procurement path, trial exit criteria, and billing kickoff
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Nick Jansen <nick@polarisai.com>, Megan Liu <megan.liu@polarisai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-10T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Polaris kickoff recap & procurement options (PO vs card / marketplace)

Hi Nick / Megan —

Thanks for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and clear next steps so we’re aligned on procurement and the trial-to-paid path. I captured our notes and a proposed kickoff cadence below.

Summary from call:
- Objective: Run a 30-day technical trial of Redwood inference integrated with Polaris’s ingestion pipeline to validate latency, cost, and quality for your conversational assistant.
- Success criteria we agreed to validate during the trial:
  * Production-ish throughput: sustained 300 concurrent requests at 1–2s expected response windows
  * Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 300ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens)
  * Cost baseline: tokens per conversation and monthly projected cost under $8k for the pilot workload
  * Quality: intent-match >= 92% on the evaluation set you shared

Procurement path options (recap):
1) Purchase Order (PO) + SOW: Polaris issues a PO to Redwood with the signed SOW attached. Typical for you if procurement requires invoice-based billing.
2) Corporate card: Fastest route; we can turn on billing immediately and invoice monthly.
3) Cloud Marketplace listing: Potentially attractive for long-term renewal; adds ~2–3 week listing lead time and requires procurement-compliant metadata.

Your stated preference: procurement team will push for PO; you wanted clarity on whether Redwood needs a signed SOW before the PO and the expected billing start date.

Proposed plan & timelines:
- Today (Jan 10): Redwood sends SOW draft, trial success metrics workbook, and a short procurement FAQ (attachments).
- Jan 11–13: Polaris legal/procurement flags contract redlines; we confirm whether a PO can be issued against the SOW or if an acceptance signature is required first.
- Jan 15: Target trial kick (access to staging keys + runbook).
- Jan 25: Proposed billing start if PO path is delayed — billing start can be pinned to the date you want us to switch from trial to paid. We recommend Jan 25 if the trial meets success criteria to avoid mid-month billing pro-ration issues.

Open questions for you / action items:
- Megan / procurement@polarisai.com: can Polaris issue a PO referencing a Redwood SOW number without a signature, or do you need a signed SOW first?
- Nick: confirm whether Polaris is interested in starting on-card if procurement timing looks like a multi-week delay.
- Rafael (CC): Redwood to provide a one-page procurement FAQ and a SOW draft by EOD today (attached).

If that plan works, Rafael and Ben will coordinate SOW edits and Marissa will own the onboarding checklist to ensure we hit the Jan 15 access target.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Director, GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Polaris_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (SOW), trial-success-metrics.xlsx (workbook), procurement-questions.docx (FAQ)
From: Nick Jansen <nick@polarisai.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Liu <megan.liu@polarisai.com>, procurement@polarisai.com
Date: 2027-01-11T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Polaris kickoff recap & procurement options (PO vs card / marketplace)

Laura —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers from our side after a procurement sync this morning:
- Procurement will accept a PO referencing the SOW; they do not require an initial signature on the SOW for issuing a PO. We can issue PO within 3–5 business days once we have the SOW number.
- That said, Legal prefers to review any non-standard terms — we’ll push back only on IP/data residency clauses if present.
- We can do corporate card to speed access for the first two weeks if Redwood is comfortable with switching billing to the PO once it lands. Is that supported?

Trial access: we can target Jan 16 for staging keys (we have an internal change freeze on Jan 15).

One more ask: can you outline the mechanism and cutoff for when you declare the trial "successful" and trigger billing? We want the criteria and who signs off.

Thanks —
Nick
Head of Product, PolarisAI
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Nick Jansen <nick@polarisai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Polaris kickoff recap & procurement options (PO vs card / marketplace)

Nick —

Yes — Redwood supports a hybrid onboarding flow: enable access immediately if Polaris pays with card, and convert invoicing to the PO once it is issued. A few implementation notes:
- Billing conversion: we can retroactively credit card charges for the trial period and have future invoices reflect the committed contract terms once PO is processed (we’ll coordinate with finance).
- Trial success declaration: joint sign-off between Polaris product lead (Nick) and Redwood CS (Marissa). We’ll use the trial-success-metrics.xlsx (attached) as the canonical yardstick. Key checkpoints: 1) functional acceptance (evaluation set pass rate), 2) performance acceptance (95th percentile latency), 3) cost acceptance (within the agreed budget band).
- If any metric fails, we’ll run a 7-day remediation plan (tuning quantization/ batching / routing policy) with no billing change until remediation completes.

Next steps (from Redwood):
- I’ll attach a cleaned SOW with an SOW number for procurement to reference (Polaris_SOW_draft_v1.pdf).
- Ben will send a short integration runbook and the staging key request form.
- Marissa will create the mutual action plan doc and calendar invites for onboarding check-ins (Jan 16 + weekly).

Ben — can you confirm runbook ETA?

—Rafael
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Nick Jansen <nick@polarisai.com>
Date: 2027-01-12T09:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Polaris kickoff recap & procurement options (PO vs card / marketplace)

Rafael / team —

Runbook ETA: Jan 12 EOD PT. It includes: staging key request URL, expected IAM roles, sample payloads, recommended batch sizes, and troubleshooting steps for common transformer OOMs. I’ll upload the runbook to the shared Drive link (see related links) and attach the staging-key-request-form to this thread.

Operational note on success criteria: please confirm who will be the signatory for the joint acceptance. Laura, can you confirm Marissa will be Redwood’s owner for sign-off? We’ll list the signatory name + email in the mutual action plan to avoid ambiguity.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
